newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe trade unions call for nationwide strike.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe trade unions call for nationwide strike.

text.p: The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) called for a two-day nationwide industrial strike starting on Tuesday after riot police stopped a planned peaceful march in support of striking medical workers on Monday.

About 50 police pounced without warning on 200 people who had gathered at the Harare magistrate court building in preparation for a march into the city centre, firing teargas and beating them with baton sticks.
Scores of other people who were streaming to join the crowd fled, with some -- choking and tears running down their cheeks -- rushing into the court building as the police gave chase.
ZCTU secretary-general Morgan Tsvangirayi and vice president Isaac Matongo who were picked up by police were later released without being charged.

Tsvangirayi told reporters the ZCTU and the Public Service Association were calling for a strike to press the government to resolve the crisis in the public health sector which has been paralysed by a three-week strike by nurses and junior doctors.
"We have decided that we should go for a national strike.... tomorrow. It will run for two days initially then we will see how it develops," Tsvangirayi told reporters.
"Our concern is if we don't do something to bring senses to these people (the government) they will never act to resolve the strike," he said.
President Robert Mugabe's government has taken a hard line against the strikers, saying it has fired them and seeking replacements from Britain, South Africa and other African states.
"It (recruiting expatriates) is not a sustainable solution. We are concerned about the situation in the hospitals. It's critical," Tsvangirayi said.

On Monday, acting Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Nathan Shamuyarira disputed statements by authorities in the country's largest hospitals, Parirenyatwa and Harare, that they had closed due to the strike.
He also said only 1,000 nurses and 100 doctors were involved while union officials say 10,000 of 14,000 nurses employed in state hospitals and 500 of 800 doctors were on the streets.

Tsvangirayi said the ZCTU was considering suing the police for violating people's constitutional rights to express themselves. "The protest march was never illegal in terms of the constitution. It's our constitutional right to express ourselves," he said.
He said he and Matongo were held for an hour until riot police had dispersed the crowd.
"It was a strategic removal from the people...They said they didn't want us to address people," he said.
